analysis_steps.goal: Build synthetic PV cuts from MHD DW solutions

method.value: Self-similar solutions scaled to physical units, power-law emissivity, convolved with Gaussian beam at 0.44 km/s sampling

evidence.quote: a parametrized emissivity function is adopted with a a simple power law radial variation

assumptions.value: Steady, axisymmetric, self-similar wind; optically thin

evidence.quote: our MHD DW model is probably too idealized (self-similar, steady, axisymmetric)

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate j_obs, r_obs, lambda_obs with three methods and compare with true values

method.value: Double-peak separation, rotation curve and flow width methods; Anderson's relation solved for r_obs

evidence.quote: we will thus consider three methods used by observers to estimate the flow specific angular momentum from PV cuts at ALMA-like resolution

analysis_steps.goal: Test predictions on HH212 ALMA data

method.value: Spectro-astrometry of blue/red centroids in 0.55" channel maps; compare PV cuts and model at 250, 70, 18 au

evidence.quote: spatial shifts much smaller than the beam can still be detected by comparing centroid positions (the so-called “spectro-astrometry" technique)

method.value: Analytic f_J = lambda_BP [1 + ln(r_out/r_in)/(2 ln(1+f_M))]^-1 applied with f_M from SO mass flux and accretion rate

results_numeric.quantity: HH212 spatial shift at z~70 au (0.55")

evidence.quote: The shift amplitude at $z \simeq 70$ au is $\Delta r \simeq 0.06"\pm 0.02"$ (27 au)
the apparent specific angular momentum in both data sets is $j_{\rm obs}$$=(\Delta r/2)(\Delta V/2)\simeq$ 27 au km s$^{-1}$
Anderson's relation yields an estimated $r_{\rm obs}$$\simeq 1$ au.
we infer an ejection to accretion ratio $f_{M,\rm obs}$ = $\dot{M}_{\rm DW}$/ $\dot{M}_{\rm in}$= 0.33 – 3.3
we obtain $f_{J,\rm obs}$ = 0.5 – 1.8

results_numeric.quantity: Flow-width method r_obs and lambda_obs (reference model, i=40)

evidence.quote: we obtain with Anderson's method $r_{\rm obs}$$\simeq 1.5$ au and $\lambda_{\rm obs}$$\simeq 2$

findings_qualitative.value: Magnetic lever arm from Anderson's formula is always a lower limit due to angular momentum in magnetic torsion

evidence.quote: The magnetic lever arm is always underestimated, due to invisible angular momentum stored as magnetic field torsion.

claims.hypothesis: Double-peak separation recovers the true outer launch radius
claims.experiment: Synthetic PV cuts of self-similar MHD DWs with varied parameters
claims.result: r_obs is always a lower limit, independent of resolution, up to factor 10 off
claims.finding: Double-peak and flow-width methods underestimate r_out; rotation curve works when resolved

evidence.quote: The "double-peak separation" method and the "flow width" method provide only a lower limit to the true outer launch radius $r_{\rm out}$.

claims.hypothesis: HH212 SO wind follows predicted biases
claims.experiment: Compare PV peak separation at 250, 65 and 18 au resolution with the MHD DW model
claims.result: j_obs ~27-30 au km/s at all resolutions, r_obs ~1 au vs r_out ~40 au
claims.finding: ALMA data confirm the predicted biases and large r_out

evidence.quote: ALMA data of HH212 confirm our predicted biases for the "double-peak separation" method

claims.hypothesis: The HH212 MHD DW can sustain disk accretion
claims.experiment: Apply analytic f_J with observed f_M
claims.finding: Enough angular momentum is extracted to sustain accretion

evidence.quote: The MHD DW candidate in HH212 extracts enough angular momentum to sustain steady accretion through the whole disk at the current observed rate.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Swept-up shell driven by an X-wind, or bowshock-shocked disk wind, cannot be ruled out

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, our proposed interpretation in terms of MHD DW is not unique.

limitations_admitted.value: Analysis is limited to self-similar steady axisymmetric models; biases may differ for other geometries

evidence.quote: While our analysis strictly pertains only to self-similar models, we expect similar biases to occur in more general geometries
